scores.evidence: Kubernetes won't let you change a Deployment selector in place.
scores.rationale: Claims about OIDC subject claims, cosign keyless identities, Argo CD adoption, selector immutability, concurrency groups and stale-approval dismissal are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: Services move over in waves, each one built in shadow first, rather than all at once.
scores.rationale: Directly sequences the 50-service migration with milestones, waves and exit criteria; exclusions (per-PR environments, portal, multi-region) are explicit and justified.

scores.evidence: Each (service, env) pair has exactly one file and one writer, deploy-bot.
scores.rationale: Clear component responsibility and data-ownership tables, a single consistent trust boundary (no cluster creds in CI), and decisions honored consistently across flows, tasks and risks.

scores.evidence: Injected bad release in staging aborted automatically by canary. 0 unsigned images admitted to prod for 2 weeks.
scores.rationale: Four spikes attack the riskiest assumptions in week 1, drills are timed against stated targets, exit criteria are measurable, and DORA metrics continue validation after launch.

scores.evidence: Everything about your current setup is an assumption. All of them are in Section 5
scores.rationale: Assumptions are tabulated with impact-if-wrong and a validation time, estimates are flagged as assumptions, and the five most design-changing unknowns are called out explicitly.

scores.evidence: Two main builds of orders-svc finish 30 seconds apart. Both run promote.yml.
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates/races, GitHub outage with break-glass, failed DB migrations with expand/contract, a bad shared-workflow release blast radius, and a concrete supply-chain threat model, each with detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Alerts: platform-failure rate > 5% over 1 hour… Each alert links to a runbook
scores.rationale: Named ownership split between platform and service teams, business-hours support sized to 4 engineers, rollback and rebuild drills, break-glass procedure, and meaningful health signals.

scores.evidence: CI minutes ≈ 500 runs × 12 min × 22 days ≈ 130k min/month, roughly $1–2k
scores.rationale: Identifies people as the dominant cost, grounds compute estimates with a stated basis and caveat to check pricing, and sets concrete controls (spending limit, lifecycle rules, monthly review).

scores.evidence: D2… Hard once 50 services use it | Security rejects in-cluster pull from GitHub → mirror the repo
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating and a revisit trigger, the hard-to-reverse ones (GitOps model, chart, config layout) get early validation, and the point of no return is explicit.

scores.evidence: Self-hosted runners (ARC) | S4 misses target, spend > $3k/month, or builds need private network access
scores.rationale: Configures existing tools rather than building, defers ARC, Backstage, per-PR environments and SLSA3 with explicit triggers, while keeping essentials like signing and canary.

scores.evidence: Changes the plan if: > 6 archetypes or > 20% unusual → add escape-hatch support in M2 and extend M2 by 2–3 weeks
scores.rationale: Day-1 steps, a dependency-ordered task table with checkable 'done when' criteria, and explicit adaptation rules if spikes disappoint; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Spike S1, service inventory… how many build archetypes exist… escape hatch for services that don't fit
Add ci.yml in shadow mode (build only) for at least 5 builds… re-enable the Jenkins deploy job
pushed to ECR as orders-svc@sha256:… ECR tags are immutable… changes the image digest in deploy-config
OIDC role per repo scoped to repo:<org>/<svc>:ref:refs/heads/main… No prod credentials exist in CI at all
Actions pinned by SHA, an organisation allowlist… cosign keyless signing… Kyverno refuses any pod whose image isn't signed
migrations must be expand/contract… Argo Rollouts canary analysis compares the 5xx rate… aborts automatically
Pact contract tests from M3… a provider can't promote if it breaks a consumer contract
Fixing flaky tests inside services. Teams own their own tests.
Mitigation: dependency and buildx layer caches. S4 measures the slowest service… p50 < 15 min
GitHub-hosted runners to start… 500 runs × 12 min × 22 days ≈ 130k min/month… org spending limit on Actions
Alerts: platform-failure rate > 5%… DORA metrics arrive in M2… Argo CD prod rebuild drill < 1 h
Every production change can be traced to a commit, an image digest and an approver… CODEOWNERS plus required review on envs/prod

traps.evidence: Services move over in waves, each one built in shadow first, rather than all at once.
ECR (immutable tags, keyed by digest)… that same digest promoted via deploy-config
No long-lived cloud keys in CI… OIDC role per repo… can only push to that service's ECR repo
Each service touches only its own files, so there are no rebase queues
CI uses GitHub Actions reusable workflows… CD uses GitOps… Argo CD

note: An exemplary, technically precise plan: pilot-first wave migration, immutable digest promotion, OIDC-scoped credentials and reversibility-aware decisions; the only notable gap is explicitly delegating flaky-test handling to service teams.
